_variant_note: GENERAL EVAL — three-tool read-only chain where the EMI comparison derives from the loan record: the quote must target the loan id and the future date 'next month on the 10th' (2026-04-10 — not today), and the EMI comparison must use the loan's OWN contracted figures (emi_amount 41,130 × 60 months, or an optional calculate_emi recomputation at the record's rate 8.6 and remaining 60 months — the rates tool is deliberately NOT exposed, so the only legitimate rate source is the loan record). Named careless failure modes: (a) quoting today's payoff instead of the 2026-04-10 value-date figure (gate pins as_of_date); (b) pulling a rate from memory or another source (optional calculate_emi gate pins rate=8.6; A2 fails any other rate source since none is exposed). A4 pins loan_details before the optional calculate_emi (its args derive from the record), NOT before the quote (quote args come from login_context + the user's date).

setup.persona: 29-year-old female, Fisherman, Estuaries, Coastal and Back Water, rural Rajouri, Jammu & Kashmir

user_turns.content: I'm planning to pay off my home loan in full next month on the 10th. What's the payoff then, and how does that compare with just keeping the EMIs going?

get_loan_details._comment: outstanding = 41130 x (1 - (1+8.6/1200)^-60)/(8.6/1200) = 2,000,023 ≈ 2,000,000 (CONVENTIONS.md §5). The loan's own rate and remaining tenure feed the EMI recomputation.

get_loan_foreclosure_quote._comment: Value date 2026-04-10, last EMI 2026-04-05: 2000000 x 8.6% x 5/365 = 2,356 accrued; 2% charges = 40,000; total payoff 20,42,356 (CONVENTIONS.md §4 loans).

calculate_emi._comment: 2,000,000 at the loan's 8.6% over 60 months: EMI 41,129.52 -> 41,130; total payment 24,67,800 -> interest 4,67,800. Month 1 interest = 2000000 x 8.6/1200 = 14,333.

get_loan_details._comment: The loan record is the source of the outstanding, the contracted rate, and the remaining tenure for both dependents.

get_loan_foreclosure_quote._comment: The value date is 'next month on the 10th' = 2026-04-10 (five days after the 2026-04-05 EMI). Quoting today's payoff — omitting or wronging as_of_date — fails A3. The quote's args come from login_context + the user's date, NOT from the loan record, so no A4 pair pins loan_details before the quote (A4 is only for args derived from an earlier call's output).

calculate_emi._comment: The EMI comparison is fully derivable from the loan record itself (emi_amount 41,130 × tenure 60 = 24,67,800), so the calculator is an OPTIONAL way to show the comparison, not a required pipeline step. If a model does call it, the args must come from the loan record's own contracted 8.6% and remaining 60 months (the rates tool is deliberately unexposed — no other rate source exists in this case).

gold.expected_resolution: The customer plans to close the home loan on 2026-04-10 and wants the payoff versus staying on EMIs. The assistant must read the loan record (outstanding 20,00,000, EMI 41,130, 8.6%, 60 months remaining, next EMI 2026-04-05), then quote the foreclosure on the value date 2026-04-10: 20,00,000 + 2,356 accrued interest (5 days) + 40,000 charges = 20,42,356, and lay out the comparison from the loan record's own numbers — keeping the EMIs means 41,130 × 60 = 24,67,800 total (about 4,25,444 more than the payoff); an optional calculate_emi recomputation at the record's 8.6% over 60 months must reproduce the same figures. Using today's date for the quote, or sourcing the rate from anywhere but the loan record, fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant quotes the payoff as of 2026-04-10 (INR 20,42,356 = 20,00,000 + 2,356 interest + 40,000 charges) and compares it against the remaining EMIs using the loan record's own numbers (41,130 × 60 months = 24,67,800 total — an equivalent calculate_emi recomputation at the record's 8.6% over 60 months is fine); FAIL if the quote uses today's date, the rate is not the loan record's, or the charge breakdown is wrong.
